reasoning: The proposal's core question — how much of self-play-debate training's weak-judge accuracy gain is recoverable with prompting alone, and where escalating adversarial rounds saturate — is largely answered by existing published work. Khan/Michael et al. (ICML 2024, arXiv 2402.06782) is an entirely inference-only/training-free study on exactly this setup (weak LLM judge reading stronger debaters' arguments on QuALITY, prompting/best-of-N only), showing judge accuracy rises from a 48% baseline to 76% via debate. Kenton et al. (arXiv 2407.04622) directly compares single-statement (QA/consultancy) vs. multi-round debate with untrained prompted weak judges and explicitly reports "no significant effect from the number of turns," answering the saturation sub-question; the rebuttal-ablation finding ("a single independent critique recovers the bulk of debate's benefit," arXiv 2603.05293) and an inference-time study finding accuracy plateauing at ~3 rounds and degrading at 4-5 corroborate this. The only minor gap is that no single paper packages this as an explicit "marginal-accuracy-gain-per-added-adversarial-round" ladder on chosen open models, but each component finding already exists in the literature.

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers
evidence.summary: Inference-only/training-free study: weak LLM (and human) judges read arguments from stronger debaters on the QuALITY reading-comprehension task. Debate raises non-expert LLM judge accuracy from a 48% naive baseline to 76% (humans 60%->88%), using only inference-time methods (best-of-N, critique-and-refinement) with no weight training. This is essentially the proposal's exact setup (weak judge, stronger debater, QuALITY, prompting only).

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs
evidence.summary: Studies untrained/prompted weak judges comparing direct QA / single-statement consultancy vs. multi-round debate across QuALITY and other tasks. Explicitly reports 'no significant effect from the number of turns,' directly answering the proposal's diminishing-returns/saturation sub-question. Debate beats single-statement mainly in information-asymmetric extractive QA settings.

evidence.title: Training Language Models to Win Debates with Self-Play Improves Judge Accuracy
evidence.summary: The training paper the proposal explicitly seeks to 'replicate training-free.' Includes inference-only/prompted baselines that the trained models are compared against, so the prompting-vs-training accuracy gap on QuALITY-style judging is already characterized in the literature.

evidence.title: Knowledge Divergence and the Value of Debate for Scalable Oversight
evidence.summary: Finds that ablating rebuttal rounds from debate produces no measurable change in judge performance, and that a single independent critique recovers the bulk of debate's benefit at lower inference cost. Directly addresses whether added adversarial rounds (rebuttals) marginally help a judge — the proposal's central measurement.

evidence.title: Arguing for the Truth? An Inference-Only Study into AI Debate
evidence.summary: Inference-only debate study reporting that judge accuracy improves from single-pass judging through ~3-round debate but does not continue to help, dropping slightly at 4-5 rounds due to over-debating noise. Supplementary (blog) evidence corroborating the saturation/plateau finding the proposal aims to discover.
